title: Systemd collector unit cowrie-firewall-events.service ran as root without filesystem, network, or capability confinement
description: Prior to remediation (commit 666bd0c), wazuh/firewall/cowrie-firewall-events.service ran /usr/bin/python3 /usr/local/lib/cowrie-lab/firewall.py as UID 0 with only NoNewPrivileges=true and PrivateTmp=true. Because journalctl -k reads local journal files and writes only to /var/log/cowrie-lab/firewall.json via StandardOutput=append, leaving root filesystem writable, full Linux capabilities, and AF_INET/AF_INET6 sockets enabled widened blast radius if the parser were ever compromised.
root_cause: The [Service] section of wazuh/firewall/cowrie-firewall-events.service omitted ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=true, ReadWritePaths=/var/log/cowrie-lab, PrivateDevices=true, PrivateNetwork=true, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX, CapabilityBoundingSet=, and AmbientCapabilities=.
intended_behavior: The firewall log collector should run with read-only host filesystem access except /var/log/cowrie-lab, zero Linux capabilities, no network namespace access, and AF_UNIX-only socket creation.

trace.description: Systemd starts Python collector as root reading kernel journal entries and appending JSON events.
Collector parses kernel log fields from journalctl stdout in the inherited service security context.
Without PrivateNetwork=true, ProtectSystem=strict, and empty CapabilityBoundingSet, a compromised worker retains host write and network capabilities.

evidence.description: Commit 666bd0c defined only NoNewPrivileges=true and PrivateTmp=true under [Service]; remediated lines 6-23 add ProtectSystem=strict, PrivateNetwork=true, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX, and CapabilityBoundingSet=.
Collector only spawns journalctl -k -f -n 0 -o cat and writes JSON lines to stdout, requiring no network sockets or write access outside /var/log/cowrie-lab.

conditions.description: Unit runs under systemd with root UID because journald kernel log access is restricted to privileged/journal readers.

execution.attacker_perspective: Code execution inside the firewall collector service inherits unrestricted capabilities, writable system directories, and host network access.
instructions: Inspect commit 666bd0c of wazuh/firewall/cowrie-firewall-events.service and compare [Service] directives against cowrie/cowrie-lab.service.
Check systemd unit sandboxing properties after applying the updated unit with systemd-analyze security cowrie-firewall-events.service.
execution.observed_result: Commit 666bd0c contained only NoNewPrivileges=true and PrivateTmp=true; after deploying the remediated unit on the VM, systemd-analyze security cowrie-firewall-events.service reports 4.1 OK and the service remains active.

remediation.strategy: Enforce strict systemd filesystem, network, device, kernel, and capability confinement on wazuh/firewall/cowrie-firewall-events.service and redeploy to the VM.

code_changes.fixed_code:
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /usr/local/lib/cowrie-lab/firewall.py
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/cowrie-lab/firewall.json
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateNetwork=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/log/cowrie-lab
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=
UMask=0027
Restart=on-failure

likelihood.reason: Input comes from local kernel nftables logs which already validate packet headers, requiring a parser flaw or local log injection.

impact.reason: Unconfined root execution allows arbitrary host file modification and outbound network access.

confidence.reason: Directly verified in git history (666bd0c) and confirmed remediated in the current unit file.

title: Unchecked IP field type allowed JSON booleans and integers to pass ipaddress.ip_address() validation
description: Prior to remediation (commit c3d614d), wazuh/telegram/custom-cowrie-telegram passed data["src_ip"] and data["dest_ip"] directly to ipaddress.ip_address(). Because Python's ipaddress.ip_address() accepts int (and bool as a subclass of int), JSON values such as true or 3232235777 were coerced into fabricated IP addresses (0.0.0.1 or 192.168.1.1) and forwarded to Telegram instead of being rejected.
root_cause: ipaddress.ip_address() accepts integer inputs in Python, and the original handler did not verify isinstance(value, str) before parsing src_ip and dest_ip.
intended_behavior: The alert formatter must accept only valid IPv4/IPv6 string representations for src_ip and dest_ip and raise ValueError for booleans, integers, or malformed strings.

trace.description: Alert JSON payload is loaded and passed into message(alert) with data["src_ip"] and data["dest_ip"].
Source and destination IP fields flow to parse_ip(value), which previously called ipaddress.ip_address(value) directly.
Coerced IP address string is embedded into the HTML Telegram alert card sent to Bot API.

evidence.description: Commit c3d614d lines 28 and 36 called ipaddress.ip_address(...) without isinstance(..., str); remediated parse_ip() at lines 44-47 enforces isinstance(value, str).
test_reject_invalid_fields verifies that src_ip=True, src_ip=2130706433, and dest_ip=3232235777 raise ValueError.

conditions.description: Occurs when a JSON alert object supplies a boolean or integer in data.src_ip or data.dest_ip.

execution.attacker_perspective: Malformed or spoofed JSON events containing boolean or numeric IP fields bypass IP format checks and emit misleading IPv4 addresses such as 0.0.0.1 in SOC notifications.
instructions: Run python -c "import ipaddress; print(ipaddress.ip_address(True), ipaddress.ip_address(3232235777))" to reproduce Python's implicit int/bool coercion.
Run python wazuh/telegram/test_telegram.py -v to verify the remediated parse_ip() check rejects boolean and integer IP inputs.
execution.observed_result: Before the fix, ipaddress.ip_address(True) returned 0.0.0.1 and ipaddress.ip_address(3232235777) returned 192.168.1.1; after adding parse_ip() with isinstance(value, str), all 7 unit tests in test_telegram.py pass and reject non-string IPs.

remediation.strategy: Require isinstance(value, str) in parse_ip() before invoking ipaddress.ip_address(), and reject bool values for rule.level and data.port_count.

likelihood.reason: Requires an upstream JSON producer or fixture to emit non-string IP fields in Wazuh alerts.

impact.reason: Produces misleading IP addresses (e.g., 0.0.0.1) in SOC Telegram notifications rather than code execution.

confidence.reason: Directly reproduced with Python ipaddress module and verified fixed by unit tests.
